reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: Common rules for AI before the strongest impose
themes.definition: Calls for international rules, oversight and governance mechanisms for AI so technology does not operate in a rule-free zone or under the rules of the most powerful.
themes.inclusion: Include passages calling for global governance mechanisms, common rules, or mutual oversight of AI/technology.
themes.exclusion: Exclude calls for UN reform (e.g. Security Council) that do not concern technology.
themes.boundary_cases: Passages framing the UN as the venue for AI rules may also be coded AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: This is precisely the task of the United Nations, to establish common rules before events or the strongest actors impose their own.
We need global governance mechanisms that ensure that such technologies respect ethical boundaries

themes.label: Algorethics and human conscience over algorithms
themes.definition: Ethical framing of AI: technology must serve humankind, respect ethical limits, and never replace human conscience or oversight.
themes.inclusion: Include references to algorethics, human-centred technology, and warnings that algorithms cannot replace human conscience.
themes.exclusion: Exclude purely institutional governance calls without ethical content.
themes.boundary_cases: Moral arguments about technology 'capable of striking' lean toward AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS if weapons are the focus; code both when ethics is the frame.

examples.quote: We must guarantee the practical application of the concept of “algorethics”, that is, ethics for algorithms.
no algorithm can take the place of human conscience

themes.label: AI control creating new domination
themes.definition: Concern that those controlling AI gain enormous advantage, producing new inequalities, dependencies, concentrations of power or domination.
themes.inclusion: Include passages warning of power concentration, dependence or domination arising from control of AI.
themes.exclusion: Exclude generic inequality statements without reference to control of technology.
themes.boundary_cases: Mentions of 'AI competition' among states without dependence or domination language go to AI_GEOPOLITICAL_COMPETITION.

examples.quote: Those who control these technologies will enjoy an enormous advantage over those who are left behind.

themes.label: Govern AI without demonizing it
themes.definition: Balanced framing that AI brings serious risks (job loss, manipulation, unsupervised decisions) yet unimaginable opportunities, so it should be governed rather than rejected.
themes.inclusion: Include passages that explicitly weigh AI's risks against its benefits and reject both fear and unregulated adoption.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages mentioning only benefits or only risks.
themes.boundary_cases: A long passage enumerating risks followed by benefits counts here, with specific risks also codable separately.

examples.quote: But governing innovation does not mean demonizing it.
Turning back is neither possible nor desirable, but neither can we hand over our future to technology without rules.

themes.label: AI competition as front of global fragmentation
themes.definition: AI rivalry among powers presented as one front of a broader breakdown of world order alongside wars, trade wars and hybrid attacks.
themes.inclusion: Include passages naming AI competition or race between states as part of geopolitical fragmentation.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages on AI dependence of small states (AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION).
themes.boundary_cases: If AI competition is only listed with no link to geopolitics, consider AI_CRISIS_LIST_MENTION.

examples.quote: nor are trade wars, AI competition, hybrid attacks, and their economic and social repercussions

themes.label: AI hub for African startups
themes.definition: Donor-country initiatives providing AI infrastructure, hubs or partnerships to build AI capacity in developing regions.
themes.inclusion: Include descriptions of AI hubs, partnerships or programmes supporting developing-country AI ecosystems.
themes.exclusion: Exclude domestic national AI strategies of the speaker's own country.
themes.boundary_cases: An AI hub described as serving sustainable development may also be coded AI_DEVELOPMENT_SDGS.

examples.quote: the opening of the AI hub for sustainable development, involving hundreds of African startups in the development of artificial intelligence

value.rationale: Italy's speeches consistently frame AI as requiring politics and common rules, with ethical (algorethics) grounding; they vary between risk enumeration, geopolitical competition, and development cooperation in Africa. One sample (2023_ITA:22) concerns Security Council reform with no AI content.
